insight.title: Why we move in a silent, shared rhythm
insight.subtitle: The invisible architecture of how we connect with one another.

sections.text: Watch a crowded street at dusk. We move like a single tide, sensing the shifts of those beside us without a word. We are masters of the unsaid. From a slight tilt of the head to a quiet smile, we spend our days reading the silent poetry written on every human face.

Our minds are built to be echoes. When you see a friend laugh, a small part of you laughs too. This inner mimicry is the secret glue of our world. We do not just observe one another; we physically feel the joys and burdens of the people we encounter every single day.

This quiet resonance is why a simple hello can change a day. We are never truly solitary islands. Every gesture is an invitation to belong. By understanding this shared pulse, we see that kindness is not just a choice, but the very language that keeps our modern world spinning gracefully together.

news.title: Vitamin B3 shows promise against MASLD, study highlights niacin’s protective role
news.description: Researchers at the Ulsan National Institute of Science and Technology report that vitamin B3 may reduce fatty liver risk by lowering microRNA-93 and restoring the protective SIRT1 gene. Published in ScienceDirect – Metabolism, the study highlights niacin’s potential role in MASLD prevention. Experts stress that further human trials are needed before clinical use.

news.title: [Isivivane Inspiration] Rooted in Makhanda: Hluma Xako’s Mission to Uplift and Encode
news.description: Hluma Xako was drawn to Computer Science because she found it a “beautifully complex” subject, one that invited her to look deeper, to understand not just how computers function, but also how they quietly power the systems that shape our everyday lives. Her academic journey reflects both curiosity and purpose: a desire to master the technical, while also understanding its impact on people and institutions.
